nodes.body: `.github/` is no longer “only an issue template” in this PR (it now also contains `copilot-instructions.md`). If the intent is to document that there are no GitHub Actions workflows, it’s clearer and accurate to reference `.github/workflows/` specifically.
Fixed in b805f64. Now points at `.github/workflows/` for the "no GitHub Actions" claim and notes `.github/` also holds `copilot-instructions.md`.

This PR adds `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, so `.github/` is no longer “only an issue template”. Consider rephrasing this gotcha to the durable point: there are no GitHub Actions workflows under `.github/workflows/`.
Fixed in b805f64. Reworded to the durable point (no workflow under `.github/workflows/`) and acknowledged `copilot-instructions.md`.

In the system-context diagram the developer is described as consuming the library as a Maven dependency, but the relationship label shows an in-repo Gradle project dependency (`implementation project(':rx2dnssd')`). That’s misleading for external consumers and also references only one module while the System node represents the whole library set.
Fixed in df87eca. Relationship label now uses a Maven coordinate form covering all three modules instead of the in-repo `project(':rx2dnssd')` notation.

On Git Bash (MINGW/MSYS), `JAVA_HOME` typically needs a slash-separated path (e.g. `C:/Program Files/...` or `/c/Program Files/...`). Using backslashes (`C:\...`) often still fails the Gradle wrapper’s `-x "$JAVA_HOME/bin/java"` check even without embedded quotes, and the verification command here should match that check.
Fixed in 28f5fe2. Example now uses a slash-separated path so it satisfies gradlew's `"$JAVA_HOME/bin/java"` check under Git Bash.

The suggested `JAVA_HOME` value uses Windows backslashes; in Git Bash this often won’t satisfy `./gradlew` because the wrapper checks for an executable at `$JAVA_HOME/bin/java`. Use a slash-separated path (and still avoid embedded quotes).
Fixed in 28f5fe2. Switched the example to a slash-separated path for the same reason as the troubleshooting.md doc.
`DNSSD` is an abstract class in the codebase (`public abstract class DNSSD`), not an interface. Calling it an interface here is misleading for contributors reading the docs.
`DNSSD` is defined as an abstract class (not an interface). The public API bullet should reflect the actual type to avoid confusion when navigating the source.
`DNSSD` is an abstract class in `dnssd/src/main/java/.../DNSSD.java`, so describing it as an interface here is inaccurate. `DNSSDBindable`/`DNSSDEmbedded` extend it rather than implement it.
`DNSSD` is not a public interface (it’s an abstract class). This bullet can be made accurate while keeping the intent (public API types use Javadoc).
In the codebase `DNSSD` is an abstract class, not an interface. The C4 component label should match the actual type.
`DNSSDBindable` and `DNSSDEmbedded` extend `DNSSD` (they don't implement an interface). Updating these relationship labels will keep the diagram consistent with the code.

This doc states consumers use Maven dependencies, but the relationship text uses a repo-local Gradle `implementation project(...)` snippet. That’s confusing in a system-context diagram; consider describing it as a Maven/Gradle dependency instead.

The sequence diagram shows `resolve()`/`queryRecords()` calling into the native library directly from `Rx2Dnssd`, but in code these go through the `Rx2Dnssd*` implementation and then `DNSSD`/`InternalDNSSD` (e.g., `Rx2DnssdCommon` calls `mDNSSD.resolve(...)` / `mDNSSD.queryRecord(...)`). The diagram should reflect that call chain.
This line says “one file per module”, but the table right below lists three test classes in `dnssd`. Consider rewording to avoid an internal contradiction.

The docs say “JDK 17 minimum”, but this repo uses Gradle 7.0.2 (wrapper) + AGP 7.0.3, so the build JDK requirement should be documented as JDK 11+ (and call out that newer JDKs may require a wrapper upgrade).

This prerequisites list hard-codes “JDK 17”, but the repo’s build is driven by Gradle 7.0.2 + AGP 7.0.3. To avoid misguiding contributors, document JDK 11+ as the requirement (and optionally note wrapper/JDK compatibility).

`[[dnssd-module]]` is an Obsidian-style wiki link and won’t be clickable on GitHub. Prefer a relative Markdown link so the module docs are navigable in the repo UI.
`[[dnssd-module]]` is an Obsidian-style wiki link and won’t be clickable in GitHub’s renderer. Use a standard Markdown link so contributors can navigate from the glossary.

This glossary row uses an Obsidian-style `[[publishing]]` link which won’t resolve on GitHub, and it also describes `DNSSD` as an interface even though it’s an abstract class in the codebase. Switching to a normal link + correcting the type will keep the glossary accurate and navigable.

Line 5 says “one file per module”, but the table below lists 3 separate test classes in `dnssd`. This reads as self-contradictory; rephrase to reflect the actual per-module test layout shown in the table.

`DNSSD` is an abstract class (extended by `DNSSDBindable`/`DNSSDEmbedded`), not an interface. Update this bullet so it matches the actual type and inheritance model.

This section describes extending the `DNSSD` “interface”, but `DNSSD` is an abstract class in this codebase. The extension guidance should reflect adding/overriding methods on the abstract base class and implementing them in both subclasses.
GitHub Markdown doesn’t resolve Obsidian-style `[[...]]` wiki links, so this reference won’t be clickable. Use a normal Markdown link to the module doc instead.

This entry describes `DNSSD` as an interface and references `[[publishing]]`, but (1) `DNSSD` is an abstract class in this repo and (2) there is no `publishing` doc in this PR, so the link won’t resolve. Update the wording and point to an actual publishing/release doc.

`DNSSD` is an abstract base class (and `DNSSDBindable`/`DNSSDEmbedded` extend it), not an interface. The diagram labels and relationships should reflect inheritance (`extends`) rather than `implements`.

`DNSSD` is an abstract class in this repo, so calling it an interface here (and listing it under “Public interfaces”) is inaccurate and may confuse contributors. Update these bullets to reflect that `DNSSDBindable`/`DNSSDEmbedded` extend `DNSSD`, while `RxDnssd`/`Rx2Dnssd` are interfaces.
